subject.size_in_frame: head and one shoulder, face about 0.22 of frame height

headroom: tight — about 0.08 of frame height above her crown, elm leaf shadow closing the top edge, so she feels pressed down into the near foreground clutter.
horizon_eyeline: No true horizon; the water-side lens at 0.30 m puts the far bank grass line across at 0.24 of frame height, high and soft behind her. Her eyeline is at 0.32 and runs diagonally down-left onto the page.

layers.fg: the open book filling the lower left quadrant, page plane large and bright, edge running out of the bottom-left corner
layers.mg: the sister's forearm and shoulder cutting across the left half of frame as a dark diagonal bar
layers.bg: the sloping bank grass and the shaded elm trunk, soft; nothing readable behind her head

gaze.note: her eyes go down-left over her sister's arm onto the page; the lead room is the page itself, so the look is answered inside the frame rather than sent out of it. She asks the line without lifting her eyes.

balance: Heavily weighted to the lower left — book and arm take two quadrants — with only her face to hold the upper right. The imbalance is the point: the page outweighs her, which is what she is complaining about.
leading_lines: The sister's forearm is the dominant diagonal, running from the left edge up to the right and delivering the eye straight to Alice's face; the book's gutter and the top edge of the page repeat it.
eye_first: The lit page bottom-left, then up the forearm to Alice's eyes.
constraint_binding: Only Alice gets a clean read: the Sister is kept to a forearm and a shoulder, no part of her face enters the frame, and no reframe gives her one.
